title: 3.5.24 Lab: Parallel-Arrays-vs-Object Refactor
description: Refactor three parallel arrays into one array of records, then read the fields back with a dot. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Start from the parallel arrays
steps.instructions: The starter keeps three separate arrays, one per field, aligned by index: a name, a score and a group for each player. Read it and see how each field is fetched from a different array at the same index.

steps.title: Collapse them into one array of records
steps.instructions: Replace the three parallel arrays with a single array called players whose elements are objects, each object holding name, score and group for one player.

steps.title: Read each record with a dot
steps.instructions: Loop over the new array and print each player's fields with bracket index then dot field, so all three fields come from one record.

requirements.title: array of object records built
requirements.description: An array holds object records: written in the brackets, pushed in one at a time, or built first in variables and listed in the brackets. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Build one array of objects, one per player, each with name, score and group. Write them in the brackets, push them in, or build each in its own variable and list them: const players = [player1, player2, player3].

requirements.title: record fields read with a dot
requirements.description: console.log prints a record's field read with a dot (players[i].name, a record variable then a dot, or a helper that returns text read off its record), or the fields are unpacked from one record with braces. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Pick a record (players[i], or the loop variable) and print each field read off it with a dot: console.log(players[i].name). A helper or a stored result counts too (checked when you press Run).

requirements.title: loop over players prints each record
requirements.description: A loop over the players array (for, for...of, while or forEach) prints something read from each record, itself or through a helper function it calls. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))
requirements.hint: Loop over players and put the console.log inside the loop, printing the current record's fields, not fixed text.

requirements.title: output printed
requirements.description: Calls console.log. Help: 3.5.9 (Objects Inside Objects and Arrays)
requirements.hint: Print with console.log so you can see the result and check it against what you expected.

requirements.title: players holds one record per player, with the same data
requirements.description: After the code runs, players is the three records { name, score, group } for Marisol, Dev and Priya, in that order. Help: 3.5.23 (A Record-Shaped Object)
requirements.hint: Build players as an array of three objects with the keys name, score and group, using the values from the old arrays in the same order. Delete the old parallel arrays.

requirements.title: the parallel arrays are gone
requirements.description: No array of plain values is left, however it is made (a list in brackets, split, Array.of, new Set): the names, scores and groups live only in players. Help: 3.5.2 (Grouping Related Values)
requirements.hint: Once players holds everything, delete the old arrays of names, scores and groups, whatever they are called. Two copies of the data can drift apart.

requirements.title: the loop prints each player from the records
requirements.description: A loop that runs prints every player's name, group and score read from players, one player per line. Typed-in text, and a loop that never runs, do not count. A printed undefined names the read that found nothing. Help: 3.3.5 (Looping Over Arrays (for / for…of))
requirements.hint: Loop over players and, inside the loop, print the current record's name, group and score read with a dot.

checks.fail: Nothing was printed by code that runs. A console.log inside a function nobody calls, or behind a test that is never true, prints nothing.
A printed line says undefined: a read found nothing. Check the spelling of each name you read.
Not every player's name, group and score is printed by the loop. Inside the loop, print the current record's fields read with a dot: players[i].name.

checks.expr: players.every(p => output.some(l => l.includes(p.name) && players.every(o => o === p || !l.includes(o.name))))
checks.fail: Print each player on a line of its own from the loop: a line that names one player should not name the others.
